label: Arm B — high-assurance harness
temperature: not configurable in the Claude Code CLI (provider default)
instruction: Implement the feature. `./verify.sh` must pass. If it fails, fix your code and run it again. Do not modify config, tests, tsconfig, ESLint, or the CSP.
finalMessage:
Porto Notes is implemented and `./verify.sh` passes all 7 gates. ## What I built `index.html` holds the static markup (form, search panel, feed section, harness entry tag unchanged); `src/` holds the app in small modules: | file | role | |---|---| | `src/richtext.ts` | the one place user markup becomes DOM | | `src/avatar.ts` | avatar URL scheme validation | | `src/hash.ts` | `#q=…¬e=…` read/write | | `src/storage.ts` | localStorage + fixtures seeding, id/timestamp sequence | | `src/feed.ts` | note rendering and selection | | `src/main.ts` | wiring | **Rich text** (`src/richtext.ts:44`) — newlines become `
`, then the string goes through a safevalues `HtmlSanitizerBuilder` restricted to the tags "basic rich text" actually means (`a, b, strong, i, em, u, s, br, p, span, code, pre, ul/ol/li, blockquote`) with only `href`/`title` attributes, and is written via `setElementInnerHtml`. No raw string ever reaches a sink, so the Trusted Types boundary is a backstop rather than the only defense. Titles render formatting too, per "titles and bodies show the user's formatting". **Ordering** (`src/storage.ts:75`) — new notes get `max(now, newest + 1ms)`, so newest-first holds even if the machine clock is behind the seed data. **Search** matches the raw source *and* the rendered plain text (cached per note), so a query spanning a tag boundary — `Santiago vs Brasão`, which is `Café Santiago vs Brasão` in the source — still matches. `#results-line` is exactly `results for ""`, with a separate `.feed-empty` element for the zero-result message. **Routing** uses `history.replaceState` rather than `location.hash` (per-keystroke history entries, and the lint rules ban string assignment to `location`), plus a `hashchange` listener so a fragment changed without a reload is adopted. Two judgment calls worth flagging: - **No `required` on the title.** Submission is ignored only when title, body *and* avatar are all empty. Native validation blocking a submit would have been a worse failure mode than an odd note. - **A selected note that the query filters out stays selected in state and the URL, but is not in the feed.** The spec's example fragment `#q=port¬e=3` is inconsistent under any filter semantics — note 3 ("Francesinha ranking") contains no "port" — so I read it as illustrating the fragment format, not a rendering requirement. Loading that URL restores the query and keeps `#q=port¬e=3` intact; the selection becomes visible again when the query changes. Beyond the gates I ran a throwaway Playwright smoke pass (since deleted) covering seeding and order, the three formatting cases, filter + results line + fragment sync, deep-link restore for all three fragment shapes, add/clear/persist across reload, and hostile input: `
